newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed lower as the market was disappointed by the lack of follow through buying in New York and the disappointment over the small tonnage in the European Union's export tender. The EU awarded only 250 tonnes in it's weekly export licenses tender, after 16,000 tonnes last week. October finished $1.70 easier at $350.90 per tonne, while December ended $1.80 weaker at $347.20. In New York raw sugar futures ended slightly lower correcting from 18 month highs seen Tuesday on a breakout of a two month-old range. However, the market remains nervous after rumors Egypt bought 60,000 tonnes on Tuesday, in addition to its tender for white sugar on Wednesday. But this is nothing which had should have any lasting impact on world market prices. October gave up 6 points to close at 12.12 cents/lb while March lost 7 points to close at 11.64 cents/lb. Fundamentally there still seems to be no reason for a major rally.

ROMANIA - Sugar imports into Romania continue soaring. Total imports in July 1996 amounted to 16,089 tonnes, up from last year's 5,766 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first 11 months of 1995/96 (September/July) up to 307,284 tonnes against 256,990 tonnes in 1994/95. Total imports in 1994/95 amounted to 275,178 tonnes compared to 293,257 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in September/July 1995/96 were Cuba with 149,548 tonnes against 91,000 tonnes, Brazil with 28,000 tonnes compared to 19,000 tonnes and Germany with 25,031 tonnes against 20,016 tonnes. Although the level of monthly imports is likely to decline from September onwards as the domestic campaign is getting underway, total imports in 1996/97 can be expected to reach once again more than 300,000 tonnes as adverse weather conditions have affected Romania's production potential.

KOREA - Sugar imports in April 1996 amounted to 114,015 tonnes, raw value, up from 81,902 tonnes in April 1995. This brought cumulative imports in the first four months of 1996 (January/April) up to 484,523 tonnes compared to 422,755 tonnes in January/April 1995. Total imports in 1995 reached 1.31 million tonnes against 1.27 million tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in January/April 1996 were Thailand with 278,955 tonnes raws against 138,239 tonnes, Australia with 179,698 tonnes compared to 222,616 tonnes and Brazil with 23,842 tonnes againt nil. Sugar exports in April 1996 amounted to 18,722 tonnes against 13,723 tonnes in April 1995. This brought cumulative exports in January/April 1996 up to 126,121 tonnes compared to 106,021 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1995 reached 247,235 tonnes against 297,572 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of destination in January/April 1996 were Indonesia with 37,800 tonnes whites against 25,122 tonnes, Hong Kong with 35,042 tonnes compared to 37,875 tonnes and Saudi-Arabia with 26,000 tonnes against nil.

USA - Sugar imports in the USA are set to reach their highest level in five years. Total imports in June 1996 amounted to 157,859 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 98,941 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first nine months of 1995/96 (October/June) up to 1.46 million tonnes against 937,462 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1994/95 reached 1.56 million tonnes against 1.81 million tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in the first three quarters of 1995/96 (October/June) were Guatemala with 241,577 tonnes raws against 67,315 tonnes, Brazil with 230,861 tonnes compared to 151,201 tonnes and the Dominican Republic with 165,524 tonnes compared to 177,875 tonnes. The largest white sugar supplier continued to be Canada with 35,344 tonnes against 56,612 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Sugar exports in June 1996 dropped to 13,691 tonnes against 28,672 tonnes in June 1995. This brought cumulative exports in October/June 1995/96 up to 238,836 tonnes against 375,406 tonnes in 1994/95. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 504,854 tonnes against 485,708 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in October/June 1995/96 were Canada with 30,388 tonnes whites, down from 112,296 tonnes, Jamaica with 28,874 tonnes compared to 19,476 tonnes and Haiti with 28,466 tonnes against 46,201 tonnes.

UK - The fifth beet test taken on September 2 confirms that recent rainfall has helped to lift root weight above last year's level and also above the five-year average. Root weight on September 2 reached 550 grams, up from 450 grams in 1995 and also up on the five-year average (1991/95) of 542 grams. Sugar content dropped to 15.44 per cent, down from 18.84 per cent in 1995 and the average value of 17.51 per cent. This resulted in a sugar weight per root of 84.9 grams, slightly up on last year's 84.7 grams but down on the five-year average of 94.8 grams. British Sugar continues to be confident that the crop will continue to improve and that average results can be expected.

The European Union awarded 250 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 43.106 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on Wednesday. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to September 4 reached 90,250 tonnes, which compares to 339,000 tonnes last year.
